examples.claim: Serve latency overhead is single-digit ms, about 1-2 ms on average (Ray 2.0.0 docs)
examples.passage: Ray Serve's latency overhead is single digit milliseconds, around 1-2 milliseconds on average.

examples.claim: About 3-4k QPS on one 8-core machine with 1 HTTP proxy actor and 8 no-op replicas
examples.passage: Serve achieves about 3-4k queries per second on a single machine (8 cores) using 1 HTTP proxy actor and 8 replicas performing no-op requests.

examples.claim: proxy_location default EveryNode runs a proxy on every node with at least one replica; HeadOnly one proxy on head; Disabled for handle-only calls
examples.passage: EveryNode (default): Run a proxy on every node in the cluster that has at least one replica actor. HeadOnly: Only run a single proxy on the head node. Disabled: Don't run proxies at all...

examples.claim: RAY_SERVE_PROXY_HEALTH_CHECK_PERIOD_S default 10.0 s and RAY_SERVE_PROXY_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S default 10.0 s
examples.passage: RAY_SERVE_PROXY_HEALTH_CHECK_PERIOD_S ... Default is 10.0. RAY_SERVE_PROXY_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S ... Default is 10.0.

examples.claim: 3 consecutive failed proxy health checks -> unhealthy and restarted; RAY_SERVE_PROXY_READY_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S default 5.0 s
examples.passage: If a proxy fails 3 consecutive health checks, the controller marks it unhealthy and restarts it... RAY_SERVE_PROXY_READY_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S ... Default is 5.0.

examples.claim: Anyscale blog: KV-cache-event replication left as future work for overhead/complexity; char-based approach chosen as baseline
examples.passage: KV cache events emitted by each replica ... at the cost of greater event handling overhead and implementation complexity. We left the exploration of this approach to future work and took the simpler, character-based, approach to set a baseline

examples.claim: RFC design: routers rank candidate replicas, locality/multiplex logic composed as mixins; zread lists FIFOMixin, LocalityMixin, MultiplexMixin
examples.passage: RFC code: 'FIFOMixin, MultiplexMixin, LocalityMixin, RequestRouter' with rank_replicas_via_multiplex/top_ranked_replicas; zread page lists FIFOMixin, LocalityMixin, MultiplexMixin and import_path
Setting num_replicas="auto" is equivalent to ... max_ongoing_requests: 5 ... max_replicas: 100

examples.claim: Four burst knobs: lower upscale_delay_s, upscaling_factor > 1, lower metrics_interval_s but <= upscale_delay_s, lower max_ongoing_requests
examples.passage: High spikes in latency during bursts of traffic: Set a lower upscale_delay_s ... If upscaling_factor > 1 ... Always set metrics_interval_s to be less than or equal to upscale_delay_s ... Set a lower max_ongoing_requests. (The post omits the doc's caution against very low metrics_interval_s such as 0.1.)

examples.claim: route_prefix defaults to '/', FastAPI routes layer on top (/my_app + /fetch_data -> /my_app/fetch_data)
examples.passage: route_prefix ... It defaults to /. ... if your Serve application has route_prefix = /my_app and you decorate a method with @app.get("/fetch_data"), then you can call that method by sending a GET request to the path /my_app/fetch_data.

examples.claim: asyncio.shield protects async calls but does not work on DeploymentHandle calls; with no await left the replica finishes and the proxy discards the response
examples.passage: the replica processes the request as usual, sends the response back to the proxy, and the proxy discards the response ... Note that asyncio.shield cannot be used on a DeploymentHandle call to prevent the downstream handler from being cancelled.

examples.claim: Upstream batch 8, downstream 6: downstream starts a partial batch of 2; downstream batch sizes should be multiples or divisors of upstream
examples.passage: first model sets max_batch_size=8 and second model sets max_batch_size=6 ... partially filled with 8 - 6 = 2 requests ... The batch size of downstream models should ideally be multiples or divisors of the upstream models

examples.claim: Cluster-level update: pending cluster becomes active once healthy, old cluster terminated, no downtime, but Kubernetes must schedule both (two) Ray clusters
examples.passage: There should not be any downtime for the application, but note that this requires the Kubernetes cluster to be large enough to schedule both Ray clusters. ... After the pending cluster is healthy, it becomes the active cluster and the previous cluster is terminated.

examples.claim: LLMConfig deployment_config defaults to {} and supports num_replicas, max_ongoing_requests, autoscaling_config, max_queued_requests, user_config, health-check/graceful-shutdown keys and request_router_config
examples.passage: deployment_config dict {} ... Supported keys: name, num_replicas, ray_actor_options, max_ongoing_requests, autoscaling_config, max_queued_requests, user_config, health_check_period_s, health_check_timeout_s, graceful_shutdown_wait_loop_s, graceful_shutdown_timeout_s, logging_config, and request_router_config.
